note: Landmark chosen for each stamp. high/medium: checked in the first research pass. supported: a source named it as the country's best known, most iconic or symbolic landmark. partly: sources confirm it as a major landmark or main sight, or frame it as the symbol of the capital or a region rather than the whole country. changed: replaced after checking. not confirmed: searches found no source backing the pick as a national landmark, so it needs review. unverified: not checked yet. Most support comes from travel and tourism sites, not formal rankings. The set is the 193 UN member states plus the Holy See and Palestine.

countries.evidence: Sources say Andorra's profile rests on skiing rather than a single landmark.
Sources present Burj Khalifa as a global icon and a symbol of UAE ambition, but mostly as the emblem of Dubai. None ranks it the single best known landmark of the whole country.
The Minaret of Jam is Afghanistan's best known UNESCO landmark and the first site the country had inscribed (2002).
Devil's Bridge National Park showcases the natural limestone arches.
Described as Tirana's signature landmark and the centre of the city for over half a century; no source ranks it first for the whole country.
Khor Virap is called one of Armenia's most revered and photographed sites, with Mount Ararat behind it. No source ranks it as the single most iconic.
Wikivoyage calls Kalandula Falls arguably Angola's most famous tourist attraction. World Waterfall Database notes it is not widely known abroad.
The Obelisco is called an iconic landmark and national historic monument by Buenos Aires tourism, but sources frame it as the emblem of the city, not confirmed as a national symbol.
Stephansdom is called the trademark and most recognisable landmark of Vienna and is Austria's tallest church. The framing is about the capital, not a national ranking.
Australia's tourism site calls it the country's most iconic cultural landmark; a recognisability study ranked it sixth worldwide. Uluru is the natural rival.
Widely treated as Baku's main modern landmark, which has displaced the Maiden Tower in promotional material. Debated as a symbol, and a city rather than national claim.
Stari Most is described as the most famous landmark of Mostar and of Bosnia and Herzegovina; UNESCO listed, rebuilt in 2004.
Main UNESCO site is the Bridgetown Historic Centre and Garrison; the Parliament Buildings sit inside it.
Described as Bangladesh's national memorial and a cornerstone of national identity, the focal point of Language Movement Day on 21 February.
Chosen as a Belgian Icon by Brussels Airlines in 2024 from over 900 submissions; widely called Brussels' most recognisable landmark.
The Bobo-Dioulasso mosque is a major mud-brick landmark and is on UNESCO's tentative list. The Ruins of Loropeni is the country's inscribed World Heritage Site.
The cathedral's own site calls it a symbol of Sofia; one source calls it a landmark of all Bulgaria, not only the capital.

The Pearl Monument was demolished on 18 March 2011, so it was replaced. Qal'at al-Bahrain (Bahrain Fort) is described as the country's most famous archaeological site and best known landmark, and has been a UNESCO site since 2005.
Karera Falls is generally described as one of Burundi's main natural attractions; no source ranks it first.
The Door of No Return in Ouidah is a memorial arch to victims of the Atlantic slave trade, about 17 m tall on the seafront.
Described as Brunei's best known landmark and one of the most photographed icons in the country.
The Gate of the Sun is called Tiwanaku's most famous monument. No source ranks it as the best known landmark of the whole country.
Widely regarded as Brazil's most iconic symbol and most famous landmark.

Only travel and tour sites support it; the Royal Tower is called the resort's most iconic structure and commentators call the resort an instant national landmark. A private resort is a weak pick for a national symbol.
Tiger's Nest is described as a national icon of Bhutan. Trongsa Dzong was also named as its most scenic fortress.
Searches found the Kasane Baobab (Prison Tree) and Baines' Baobabs, but no source names a Chobe baobab as Botswana's best known landmark. The pick is vague and should be narrowed or replaced.
Called one of the most recognisable symbols of Belarus, a UNESCO site since 2000 and on the 50 rouble banknote.
Xunantunich is called one of Belize's most famous Maya sites and El Castillo is its best known feature; Caracol's Sky Temple is taller.
Tourism Ontario and Narcity call it Canada's most recognisable and celebrated landmark. It is also the Toronto skyline icon.
Mount Nyiragongo is an active volcano near Goma whose lava lake draws hikers.
Boali Falls is a well known landmark near Bangui (about 50 m high), shown on a 1963 stamp.
A travel source calls the Basilique Sainte-Anne one of the most important landmarks of the Republic of the Congo (green tile roof, completed 1943).
Switzerland Tourism calls the Matterhorn the symbol for Switzerland and its most famous landmark.

countries.chosen: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
countries.evidence: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace is described as the world's largest church (dome about 158 m). A major landmark, not described as a national symbol.
The moai are called Easter Island's most famous landmark and the island is a UNESCO site (1995), but it is a remote territory and sources do not rank them as Chile's top landmark.
The country's highest peak and most prominent natural landmark; the 'national symbol' wording comes from travel articles, not an official source.

countries.why: Described as the most celebrated symbol of China.
cues: wall that rises and dips along a ridge

countries.evidence: The clock tower is the gateway to Cartagena's walled city and its most recognisable landmark; sources frame it around Cartagena, not the whole country.
Called the most famous of Costa Rica's volcanoes and one of its most visited natural attractions. The volcano has been dormant since about 2010.
One source calls El Capitolio the most famous landmark in Cuba; others call it Havana's most recognised building.
Pico do Fogo is widely described as the most iconic landmark of Cabo Verde and the country's highest peak.
Described as one of Cyprus's best known landmarks and the legendary birthplace of Aphrodite; no source ranks it first.
Called the largest and most important church in Czechia and a symbol of Czech faith; Prague Castle and Charles Bridge compete as national icons.

countries.why: A symbol of reunified Germany. The travel sources more often list the Berlin Wall, Cologne Cathedral and Neuschwanstein Castle.

countries.evidence: The chimneys are Lake Abbe's signature feature and widely promoted, and the area is on UNESCO's tentative list. Lake Assal and the central market compete for top attraction.
Several guides call it Copenhagen's top attraction and one calls it Denmark's most famous landmark.
Sources lead with Morne Trois Pitons National Park (UNESCO) and the Boiling Lake. Trafalgar Falls was not named in the results.
The oldest cathedral in the Americas (founded 1511) in the UNESCO listed Colonial Zone; no source ranks it as the country's best known landmark.
Maqam Echahid is a 92 m concrete monument (opened 1982) of three palm-leaf shapes over an eternal flame, overlooking Algiers. Confirmed as a major landmark; not shown to be the top national one.
Described as the best known landmark of the Quito area, the monument to the Equator.
The Gothic town hall is the only one surviving in the Baltic and Nordic countries, with Old Thomas on the spire called Tallinn's symbol. A UNESCO Old Town landmark, but framed around the capital.
Sources consistently name the Pyramids of Giza as Egypt's most iconic landmark; the only surviving ancient wonder and a World Heritage Site.
The Fiat Tagliero Building (1938, aircraft shaped petrol station) is the standout of Asmara, a UNESCO World Heritage city.

countries.why: Spain's most visited monument and the standout pick in the travel sources.
cues: tall central tower topped with a cross

countries.evidence: UNESCO site since 1978; Bete Giyorgis, the cross shaped church, is named the most famous of the eleven churches.
Official tourism listings call it the symbol of Helsinki as a whole; the claim is about the capital rather than the country.
Widely described as one of Nadi's best known landmarks and the largest Hindu temple in the Southern Hemisphere. No source calls it Fiji's top landmark.
Nan Madol is the best known site in Micronesia and the first inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List (2016).

countries.why: The best known symbol of France, named as such across the sources.

countries.evidence: The best known attraction of Ivindo National Park and one of the most powerful waterfalls in Central Africa; remote, and no source calls it the national icon.

countries.why: The sources gave the weakest evidence for the UK. Big Ben only appeared in a photo caption, so this pick rests on general recognition.

countries.evidence: The main landmark of St George's, the capital, built by the French in 1706 to 1710.
Georgia's tourism site calls it one of the most recognisable monuments in the country; guides call it a symbol of Georgia.
A UNESCO site and one of Ghana's most visited historic monuments, best known for the Door of No Return. Elmina Castle is the other major slave castle.
Arch 22 in Banjul (built 1996, about 35 m) is a well known landmark. One guide calls it a UNESCO site, which looks like a mix up with Kunta Kinteh Island.
Called the signature landmark of the region and a UNESCO natural site, but it sits on the Guinea, Liberia and Cote d'Ivoire border so it is shared.
Called Malabo's best known landmark and the country's most important Catholic church. One report mentions a fire at the cathedral; the date and damage were not confirmed.
Sources describe the Parthenon as Greece's most iconic and recognisable landmark; the Acropolis is a UNESCO site.
Temple I is called the most recognised structure at Tikal and appeared on the 50 quetzal note; Tikal is a UNESCO site (1979). One source ranks Temple IV as the most iconic.

countries.chosen: Fortaleza de Sao Jose da Amura
countries.evidence: One of Bissau's main landmarks and the site of the Cabral mausoleum. Still a military site, with restricted access.
Called Guyana's most iconic landmark; featured on banknotes.
Copan Ruins is the top listed landmark in the guide found.
The walls are called the main landmark of Dubrovnik and a UNESCO listed site (1979). The claim is about the city; Croatia has other headline sights.
Described as Haiti's best known landmark and a symbol of independence; shown on its currency and stamps, and a UNESCO site since 1982.
Called Budapest's most iconic landmark and a symbol of national identity; it houses the Crown of St Stephen.
National Geographic Traveller calls it Indonesia's most famous landmark; the world's largest Buddhist temple and a UNESCO site (1991).
Ireland's most visited natural attraction in 2022 (about 1.1 million visitors). Evidence of popularity rather than a source naming it the top national symbol.
UNESCO site (2001) and among Israel's most visited attractions, roughly second to Jerusalem. Politically sensitive picks are easy to swap.
Sources consistently call the Taj Mahal India's most iconic landmark; the only Indian monument in a top 10 Travellers' Choice landmarks list.
Called Samarra's most famous landmark and a treasured Iraqi national monument. The top was damaged in 2005; UNESCO restoration began in 2017.
Widely treated as the symbol of Tehran; the monument's director calls it a national symbol of Iran, though it is described as a contested one (built 1971 as Shahyad).
Described as Reykjavik's most recognisable landmark, visible across the city; the claim is about the capital.

countries.why: Used in your reference image. The Colosseum ranks higher in recognition surveys (4th worldwide), so it is the main alternative.

countries.evidence: Lonely Planet calls it Jamaica's top-grossing tourist attraction; other guides call it the country's most famous attraction.
The Treasury is called Petra's most iconic monument; Petra is the country's flagship UNESCO site. The Monastery is a rival within Petra.

countries.why: Matches your reference image. Mount Fuji appears in the sources as an iconic landmark.
cues: two pillars with curved top beam

countries.evidence: Mount Kenya appears on the national coat of arms and is a UNESCO site, so it is a national symbol, but no source ranks it Kenya's single most famous landmark.
Burana Tower, the minaret stump of a destroyed city.
Angkor Wat appears on the national flag.
The maneaba is the central cultural institution of Kiribati and the national parliament is called the Maneaba ni Maungatabu. It is a building type rather than one landmark.
Mount Karthala is the highest point of the Comoros and an active volcano on Grande Comore.
Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park is a UNESCO site.
One of Pyongyang's best known monuments, completed 1982 for Kim Il Sung's 70th birthday; described as a national symbol in some sources.
The main gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace, described as a symbol of Seoul's Joseon history and a cultural icon. Results did not rank it nationally.
Described as Kuwait's national symbol and capital landmark, shown on the old 1 dinar note; it won the Aga Khan Award in 1980.
Described as a symbol of the whole country, compared in status to Big Ben or the Eiffel Tower, and shown on the 10,000 tenge note.
Called the national symbol of Laos and its most important national monument.
The Temple of Jupiter is the centrepiece of the UNESCO listed Baalbek complex (1984); sources did not rank Baalbek against other Lebanese sights.
The Pitons Management Area near Soufriere.
Vaduz Castle is the most frequently named landmark.
Called one of Sri Lanka's most visited and best known sights and a UNESCO site since 1982. Most support is from travel sites.
No source supported the lighthouse. Sources name the J.J. Roberts Monument, Centennial Pavilion and Providence Island. Switched to the Roberts Monument; no single agreed landmark.
The mokorotlo (Basotho hat) is on the national flag; the Mokorotlo Building in Maseru is described as Lesotho's most striking architectural landmark.
Sources call it a symbol of Lithuania and probably its most famous castle; a Gothic island castle on Lake Galve.
Sources named Vianden Castle as a picturesque landmark; the Adolphe Bridge was not mentioned. Vianden Castle is the likely alternative.
Widely regarded as a national symbol of freedom and independence, unveiled in 1935 and still the focus of official ceremonies.
The Arch of Septimius Severus is a key landmark of Leptis Magna, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
Described as Morocco's most iconic landmark in travel sources, with a 210 m minaret. Built in 1993 to give Casablanca a major landmark; sources are mostly travel sites.
Monte Carlo Casino is the most cited attraction.
Reported as the most visited site in Moldova outside the capital; the cave monastery is its centrepiece.
The fortifications are the top attraction of Kotor and sit in a UNESCO listed site; Kotor is one of several headline sights in Montenegro.
Travel sources call it the most iconic sight in Madagascar. The Tsingy rock formations are the main rival.

Majuro Atoll is a place, not a landmark, and no source gives it as a national symbol. The Capitol complex in Delap is described as the main symbol of statehood. The pick should be replaced with a specific structure.
A 66 m cross on Mount Vodno, one of the best known landmarks of Skopje; its role as a national symbol is politically contested.
Called the defining landmark of Djenne and widely regarded as the largest mud built structure in the world; sources did not rank it against other Malian sites.
Called Myanmar's most famous landmark and its holiest Buddhist site.
A major landmark east of Ulaanbaatar and a Guinness record statue, completed 2008. No source ranks it Mongolia's top landmark.
Sources identify the mosque and minaret as Mauritania's national emblem and it appears on the 1000 ouguiya note; restoration is under way.
The Azure Window, Malta's best known rock formation, collapsed. Valletta skyline kept as a stand-in.
Travel sources call it Mauritius's most iconic landmark; UNESCO listed in 2008 for its maroon heritage. Support is from travel pages, not an official ranking.
The Islamic Centre with its golden dome is called Male's best known landmark and the most recognisable feature of the skyline; the claim is about the capital.
Mulanje is the main attraction of southern Malawi, holds Malawi's highest point (Sapitwa, 3,002 m) and was added to UNESCO's list in 2025. No source ranks it first nationally.

countries.why: A New Seven Wonders site. The Teotihuacan pyramids lead one source, with Chichen Itza close behind.

countries.evidence: Described as Malaysia's leading national symbol and most renowned icon; the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
Called Maputo's most famous landmark and ranked by publications among the world's most beautiful railway stations; a city rather than national claim.
Travel sources call Sossusvlei easily Namibia's most iconic destination. Deadvlei within it is also named the most iconic landmark.
The 27 m mud brick minaret is called the city's landmark and one of Niger's best known, in the UNESCO listed historic centre of Agadez.
Known as the gateway to Abuja and shown on the 100 naira note. Sources are mostly tourism pages and none ranks it Nigeria's top landmark.
Results named the Isletas of Granada and Mombacho Volcano; Momotombo was not mentioned.
The pick is generic. Windmills are listed with clogs, cheese and bicycles as the most recognisable Dutch symbols, and Kinderdijk is the UNESCO site (1997) with 19 mills.
Called the most famous of Norway's stave churches and the only one on the UNESCO list (1979). Stave churches as a type are a national icon; Urnes is not ranked against fjord sights.
Called one of Kathmandu's most iconic landmarks and among the largest stupas in the world (UNESCO 1979); not ranked above Swayambhunath.
The pinnacles of Topside, left by phosphate mining, cover about 80 percent of the island and are called its most defining sight; support is from travel pages.
New Zealand's highest mountain (3,724 m) and a UNESCO site since 1990, described as a national icon in mostly travel sources; no formal ranking.
Called one of Oman's most iconic landmarks; opened 2001, the country's tallest structure with a 90 m minaret, and open to non-Muslim visitors.

Sources describe a road bridge (1962) over the Pacific end of the canal, not a national symbol. The Panama Canal itself, for example the Miraflores Locks, is the more likely icon and should be considered.
Treated as Peru's most famous landmark and the main emblem of the Inca Empire; UNESCO site since 1983 and one of the New Seven Wonders (2007).
Described as a major symbol of PNG identity; the national parliament in Port Moresby is modelled on it. It is a Sepik region building type rather than one landmark.
Described as the Philippines' most iconic volcano for its near perfect cone; on the tentative World Heritage list. No source ranks it first among all national landmarks.
Called one of Lahore's most iconic landmarks, completed 1673 by Aurangzeb; the claim is about the city rather than the nation.
Warsaw's best known and most visible landmark and the tallest building in Poland. A divisive Soviet era gift (1955) rather than a clear national symbol.
Jerusalem's most recognised landmark and a symbol of Palestinian national aspiration in popular and political use, though not an official emblem and claimed by both sides. Politically sensitive pick.
Called Lisbon's most iconic landmark and one of Portugal's most famous; seen as a metonym for Portugal and the Age of Discoveries. UNESCO site.
The Rock Islands Southern Lagoon is Palau's UNESCO site and a leading dive destination; its most famous single attraction is Jellyfish Lake. Pick is an area rather than one landmark.
One list named Itaipu Dam as Paraguay's landmark. The Jesuit Missions of Trinidad (UNESCO) is kept.
Described as a landmark of Doha built for the 2006 Asian Games and a 2008 CTBUH award winner; sources disagree on whether it is still the tallest.
Called Romania's most famous landmark and best known medieval castle; its Dracula link is myth, since Vlad the Impaler never lived there.
Called the most recognisable building in Belgrade, with a dome modelled on Hagia Sophia and dedicated to the nation's patron saint. The claim is about the capital.
Described as Russia's most recognisable symbol and compared to the Eiffel Tower for France; completed 1561 and a UNESCO site.
Volcanoes National Park is called Rwanda's most famous national park and top attraction, mainly for the mountain gorillas. The Virunga range is shared with Uganda and the DR Congo.
One of Riyadh's best known landmarks, 302 m tall, and called an icon for the whole country by the architect firm. Not ranked against other Saudi sites.
The highest peak in the Solomon Islands (about 2,335 m) on Guadalcanal, but no source calls it a famous or symbolic landmark. A weak pick that should be reconsidered.
Lonely Planet calls it one of the most photographed beaches on the planet and travel sites call it the most photographed in Seychelles; no hard data behind the superlative.
UNESCO listed in 2011 and once called Sudan's most visited heritage site, but sources do not rank it Sudan's most famous. Preservation work has halted because of the current war.
Called the most famous symbol of Stockholm, with a tower topped by the Three Crowns national emblem and the Nobel dinner venue. Framed around the capital.
Travel and blog sources call it Singapore's most recognisable landmark; the Merlion is the frequent rival and no source gives a formal ranking.
Called the most recognisable symbol of Bled island and appears on many postcards; the image is a Slovenia icon but sources frame it around Bled.
Called the most recognisable symbol of Bratislava; framed around the capital.
A confirmed national symbol, on banknotes and stamps. It was felled by a storm on 24 May 2023, so the stamp shows a landmark that no longer stands.
The Three Towers are the iconic sight.
At 49 m the tallest statue in Africa (inaugurated 2010) and called one of Dakar's most visited sites. A controversial vanity project to critics.
A 13th century mosque in Mogadishu, damaged in the civil war and restored since 2017, but no source names it Somalia's best known landmark.
Major landmark of Paramaribo's UNESCO listed historic inner city; an all wooden cathedral.
Mount Kinyeti (3,187 m) in the Imatong Mountains is the country's highest point, but no source presents it as a famous or symbolic landmark. A weak pick.
The CIA World Factbook identifies it as the country's most famous landmark; a 663 m volcanic plug often described as the national emblem.
Results named Joya de Ceren and Tazumal; Izalco volcano was not mentioned.

The Great Colonnade is part of the UNESCO listed Site of Palmyra (1980), which is on the Danger list; sources do not rank the colonnade as the most famous feature, and parts of the site were destroyed in the conflict.
A major granite landmark near Mbabane, called the world's second largest exposed monolith; the local lager is named after it. No ranking against other national sights.
The Aloba Arch is described as the best known feature of the UNESCO listed Ennedi Massif (2016). The pick says only Ennedi Arch, which is ambiguous among several arches.
UNESCO describes the Batammariba tower houses (takienta) as a symbol of Togo.
Called one of Bangkok's defining landmarks and shown on the 10 baht coin. Other Thai sights such as the Grand Palace also compete.
Called a famous landmark of Tajikistan and shown on the 20 somoni banknote. The visible fortress has been rebuilt recently.
Called the capital's best known landmark: a 27 m statue unveiled 1996 as an Indonesian gift, later kept by the independent state. Its origins are contested.
Presented as a symbol of Turkmen statehood and neutrality (recognised 1995), centre of Neutrality Day celebrations. The monument was moved in 2010.
The Ministry of Cultural Affairs calls it the most accomplished Roman monument of its kind in Tunisia; UNESCO site since 1979. Carthage competes for national fame.
Tonga's best known monument, a coral limestone trilithon at Niutoua on Tongatapu. Location corrected.

countries.why: Istanbul is the headline destination. The sources name Istanbul, Pamukkale, Cappadocia and Ephesus, with no single national symbol.

countries.evidence: The first of the Magnificent Seven mansions around Queen's Park Savannah in Port of Spain, a well known group; no source ranks it as the country's top landmark.

Funafuti Atoll is a place, not a landmark. Sources name the Fetu Ao Lima (Morning Star Church) as its most prominent building and Government House as a symbol of self-governance; none names a national landmark. The pick should be replaced with a specific structure.
Travel sources call Kilimanjaro the most recognisable and iconic landmark in Tanzania and Africa's highest mountain; UNESCO site since 1987. The currency and emblem claim is from secondary sources.
A UNESCO site (1990) in Kyiv, on the Danger list since 2023 and damaged by a strike; sources describe its heritage status but do not rank it Ukraine's top landmark.
UNESCO site (2001) and burial ground of the Buganda kings. The main hall burned in 2010, was restored and the site left the Danger list in 2023. No source ranks it Uganda's top landmark.

countries.why: Ranked first in a worldwide recognition survey (98.7 percent could identify it).

countries.evidence: The city of Montevideo's own tourism site calls its tower an iconic symbol of the city; travel guides call it the most iconic building. Framed around the capital.
One guide calls it the symbol of Samarkand and, arguably, the most recognisable landmark in Uzbekistan.
St Peter's Basilica is the main landmark.
The highest point of the country and its most prominent natural landmark; erupted in April 2021 and its national park is on the UNESCO tentative list.
Called Venezuela's signature natural landmark and shown on its banknotes; the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall. In 2009 the president called it the nation's most famous landmark.
Vietnam's first natural UNESCO site (1994), named among the world's most beautiful natural wonders in press coverage. Sources do not rank it against other Vietnamese sights.
Mount Yasur described as the most iconic landmark of Tanna.
A well known landmark at Tiapapata near Apia, dedicated 1984 and called the Mother Temple of the Pacific Islands; no source ranks it Samoa's top landmark.
Known as the Manhattan of the Desert for its mud brick towers up to 11 stories; UNESCO site, on the Danger list since 2015.
South African Tourism calls it South Africa's most iconic landmark and one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature.
Described as Zambia's top attraction and a UNESCO site (1989), shared with Zimbabwe.
The ruins gave the country its name and the Zimbabwe Bird found there is the national emblem on the flag and arms; shown on currency and UNESCO listed (1986).
